grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them on the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
observed.evidence: Setup: 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused cards unseen.

grades.reason: Neutral independent Q01 adjudication: The used Conflict cards are placed/dealt face down to form the deck. Neither the answer nor its same-response evidence states this state or an equivalent concealed-deck instruction.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: In four players, a human starts at 1 VP; in other player counts including three, at 0 VP. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and a third Swordmaster Agent beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup, step 6: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents; third beside board; three troops in garrison, nine in supply; take 1 water.

grades.reason: Correct 4P/3P starting scores, available and set-aside Agents, three garrison/nine supply troops, and one water.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: You may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the cards just revealed from your remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Player Turns and Reveal Turn: Agent turns optional; once Revealed, turns skipped; resolve revealed cards only; Clean Up all cards.

grades.reason: Permits early Reveal, bars later Agent turns, restricts Reveal effects to remaining hand, and discards all played cards at cleanup.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can pay the entry cost if gained before entry. Resources from the card being played to send the Agent or from the destination itself cannot pay that same entry cost; entry is paid before those effects. One card sends only one Agent using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn and may only be revealed.
observed.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement may grant entry resources; later gains cannot pay that entry. Agent Turn: choose only one icon; no icons means Reveal only.

grades.reason: Correctly separates pre-entry Plot resources from later Agent-card/space gains, limits one card to one Agent/icon, and excludes no-icon Agent plays.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited that turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison: at most five troops. At a non-Combat space, the troops recruited go into your garrison and cannot be deployed there. Recruited troops come from your supply; if it is empty you cannot recruit more until troops return to it.
observed.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison at Combat spaces; recruit from supply; garrison units do not help Combats.

grades.reason: Correct maximum five (three new plus two old), no ordinary noncombat deployment, and recruitment from personal supply.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at the destination, not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card, chosen just after placing your Agent and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though different Spies may do each on one placement.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather timing; cannot recall same Spy for both.

grades.reason: Correct Spy-icon access without recall, connected own-Spy Infiltrate, Gather draw and immediate timing, and prohibition on using one Spy twice.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2, plus 1 sandworm × 3, plus 4 revealed swords × 1 = 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict has strength 0 and cannot play Combat Intrigue because only players with at least one unit may do so.
observed.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no units means strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

grades.reason: Correct strength eleven, zero after the last unit is removed, and unit requirement for Combat Intrigue participation.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
observed.evidence: Combat Intrigue: may play after earlier pass; resolve once all involved pass consecutively. Cleanup returns troops to supply, worms to bank, markers to 0.

grades.reason: Correct permission to act after passing, consecutive-pass closure, troop-to-supply and worm-to-bank destinations; also resets markers.

grades.question: Compare two players tied for first in a four-player Conflict with the same tie in a three-player Conflict. Who takes the Conflict card, and can a zero-strength player get a reward?
grades.expected: Each tied first gets second reward and nobody wins or takes card. In four-player game remaining players compete for third; in three-player game no further rewards. Zero strength never rewarded.

observed.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player gets the second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
observed.evidence: Combat ties by player count; Resolve Combat: zero strength receives no reward.

grades.reason: Correct second rewards for tied leaders, 4P third-reward competition versus no further 3P rewards, no winner/card, and no zero-strength reward.

grades.question: What does a sandworm do to rewards: do two sandworms quadruple them, can control or battle icons double, and how is a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP handled?
grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. If the reward lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice a second time to gain the VP a second time (6 spice for 2 VP total).
observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more doubles; location control and battle icons excluded; may pay optional cost again.

grades.reason: Correct single doubling regardless of worm count, control/icon exclusions, and paying six spice rather than receiving a free second VP.

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it for a matching battle icon against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. If a match exists, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three icon types in your supply, for 1 VP when the pair is flipped.
observed.evidence: Winner takes Conflict card face up, then mandatory match check; Battle Icons section lists face-up cards and wild Endgame match.

grades.reason: Correct post-acquisition match check, face-up Conflict/Objective eligibility, mandatory pair flip for one VP, and Endgame wild use.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; dropping below 2 loses it and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which is tied to holding it. Tying the holder does not take the Alliance; a challenger must rise above the holder.
observed.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence: 2 and 4 rewards/reversal; tying does not steal; rising above transfers.

grades.reason: Correct reversible two-Influence VP, retained and repeatable four-Influence track bonus, holder-dependent Alliance VP, and no theft by a challenger merely tying.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

observed.answer: During Reveal you may spend gained Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from sources to buy one card and split one source across cards. The Imperium Row is replenished to five cards, so you can buy the replacement immediately if able. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards: timing, pooling/splitting, replacement, acquired card to discard.

grades.reason: Correct Reveal purchase interleaving, pooling/splitting, immediate replacement purchase, and acquired-card discard destination.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

observed.answer: At a Maker space with no Agent during Makers, add 1 spice to its bonus spot, accumulating with previous bonus spice; visiting gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Sandworms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; removing it permits summoning to any Conflict. Hooks are only required when the effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A worm is placed directly in the Conflict, never a garrison.
observed.evidence: Makers; Deep Desert/Hagga Basin board table; Sandworms and Shield Wall rules; FAQ says Hooks retained.

grades.reason: Correct Maker accumulation/collection, specified Hooks prerequisites, protected Conflicts while Wall remains, and direct Conflict placement rather than garrison.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: At Recall, if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: Endgame timing, Endgame Intrigue, winner and tiebreak order.

grades.reason: Correct end-of-round Recall trigger, Endgame Intrigue before VP comparison, and spice/Solari/water/garrison tiebreak order.

grades.question: With optional standard CHOAM, how many contracts start face up and face down, which extra cards are added, is Shaddam compulsory, and are the 10 contrasting-back contracts part of this standard setup?
grades.expected: 20 standard contracts: two face up, eighteen in bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium; Shaddam optional. Ten contrasting-back contracts are only Rise of Ix compatibility, excluded from standard setup.

observed.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts; expose 2 face up and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 additional Intrigue cards to that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards to that deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader choice, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix and are left in the box; standard CHOAM uses all 20 standard contracts.
observed.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and contrasting-back contracts note.

grades.reason: Correct two face-up/eighteen face-down standard contracts, four extra cards of each deck, optional Shaddam, and excluded ten Ix contracts.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: Take one of two face-up into supply then refill face up from bank; if all taken gain 2 Solari (also without module). Harvest: visit Maker and gain specified total spice that turn including other sources. Immediate upon taking. Acquire The Spice Must Flow on next acquiring that card.

observed.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken, it instead gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes when you send an Agent to a Maker space and gain the contract's specified spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts: Harvest, Immediate, Acquire The Spice Must Flow.

grades.reason: Correct taking/refilling offers, exhausted-contract Solari fallback, and distinct Harvest/Immediate/next-Spice-Must-Flow completion conditions.

grades.question: You gain a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn. Can you complete it now? Once completed what do you announce, gain and do with the token?
grades.expected: Cannot complete now; must have held contract when Agent sent, wait future turn. Announce completion, gain printed rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

observed.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already placing your Agent at that space this turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
observed.evidence: Completing contracts: already-visited space must wait; FAQ says announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

grades.reason: Correct rejection of retroactive space-contract completion and announce/reward/face-down-in-supply procedure.

grades.question: In standard two-player play how many Rivals are used, who gets the Ornithopter Objective, who gets First Player, what is the turn order, and does a Rival Reveal?
grades.expected: One shared Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective, other two randomly humans; Rival never First Player. Marker alternates humans, Rival considered clockwise from First Player and acts between humans each round. Takes Agent turns while it has Agent in supply, never Reveals.

observed.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to humans, and the human whose Objective shows First Player gets the marker. First Player alternates only between humans. Each round order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

grades.reason: Correct one shared Rival, Rival Ornithopter, marked human First Player alternating between humans, intervening Rival order, and no Rival Reveal.

grades.question: A Rival reveals an occupied board space, then a Place Spy card. How does it proceed, which space costs and effects apply, and what happens when House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle is drawn?
grades.expected: Occupied: ignore and reveal again. Place Spy tries empty designated post, ignore placement if none, then reveal another card regardless because no Agent sent. Ignore normal space costs/effects; use Hagal effects only. Empty deck or Reshuffle: immediately reshuffle Hagal and continue.

observed.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, and immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore normal destination costs and effects; apply only the revealed Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; empty deck/Reshuffle procedure.

grades.reason: Correct skip/reveal procedure for occupied destinations and non-Agent Spy cards, Hagal-only effects, and immediate reshuffle handling.

grades.question: How are eligible Objective cards selected and distributed in standard three- or four-player setup, how is First Player chosen, and may Shaddam be chosen without CHOAM?
grades.expected: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P or 4/6P mark mismatches count; shuffle, each takes one random face up in supply. First Player is holder of marked Objective. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.

observed.answer: Shuffle Objective cards after removing those whose 1–3P/4/6P marking does not match the player count; distribute one eligible card face up to each player. The marked Objective identifies First Player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so he cannot be chosen without it.
observed.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; omit mismatched Objectives, distribute face up, marked Objective determines First Player.

grades.reason: Correct player-count filtering, shuffled face-up Objective distribution, marked First Player, and Shaddam restriction.

grades.question: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water or sandworms, what happens? Contrast an empty personal troop supply, and state where resource payments go.
grades.expected: Bank resources and sandworms not limited; substitute conveniently. Cannot recruit troops from empty personal supply until returned. Resource gains come from bank and payments return to bank.

observed.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; if they run out, make any convenient substitution. If your personal troop supply runs out, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Gain Solari, spice, and water from the bank; payments of those resources go back to the bank.
observed.evidence: Setup step 7: substitutions if bank runs out; resources taken from/returned to bank. Recruit section: empty troop supply prevents recruitment.

grades.reason: Correct unlimited bank substitutions versus finite personal troops and bank destinations for gains/payments.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

observed.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict and place it face up on top of any unclaimed earlier Conflict cards, resolve control's defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if no Endgame, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start another round.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure phases; Round Start and Recall descriptions.

grades.reason: The unrestricted Recall request is within standard2–4-player scope and the original fixed key explicitly includes the two-player Rival exception. Must state that First Player alternates only between humans, never Rival, and distinguish restoring Rival Agents to supply. Generic recall-to-Leaders/pass-clockwise alone omits the material2P procedure. NEW full14 and independent neutral14 agree; no cross-answer borrowing or literal-keyword requirement.

grades.question: May you resolve board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order? Can you use that visit’s Influence to meet its entry requirement?
grades.expected: Resolve effects in any order after placement, but entry requirements and costs must be met before any effects. Cannot rely on Influence gained by the visit for its entry requirement.

observed.answer: Yes. After paying costs and meeting requirements, you may resolve board-space and Agent-box effects in any order, and advance Influence for the Faction space. No: entry costs and requirements must be met before effects of the space or played card, so the visit's Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
observed.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; effects may be carried out in any order.

grades.reason: Correct post-entry freedom of effect order and inability to use visit-generated Influence for that visit's prerequisite.

grades.question: Can an optional arrow cost be paid twice in an Agent turn? Which effects are normally optional or mandatory, including costs on Intrigue cards?
grades.expected: Only once per turn, except sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards. Most effects mandatory except may, optional arrow payment and black-X trash. Direct self-trash mandatory. All Intrigue conditions/costs required to play it.
grades.source_references: Main pp9,20; FAQ p3 optional effects/paying a cost

observed.answer: No. An arrow cost and its effect can be used only once per turn, even if you have enough resources to repeat it; sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
observed.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

grades.reason: Correct once-per-turn arrow limit and doubled-Conflict exception, mandatory default, optional may/arrows/black-X trash, and required Intrigue costs.

grades.question: Where may a new Spy be placed, what if all your Spies are already deployed, and what if its placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type?
grades.expected: Unoccupied observation post, from supply. If none in supply may first recall one of own Spies for no effect. Specified icon must connect to post or cannot place there.

observed.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to that post, you must satisfy it or cannot place there.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post; may recall if supply empty; specified Agent icon constraint.

grades.reason: Correct unoccupied post from supply, free recall if own supply empty, and connection restriction for a specified Agent-icon type.

grades.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?
grades.expected: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: No. Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent only, not your own. You still must play a card for an Agent turn; recalling a Spy does not itself send an Agent. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement; you may use one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ—Spies: recall requires card, two different effects allowed, never two Gather Intelligence.

grades.reason: Correctly rejects own-Agent Infiltrate, cardless Agent turns, and duplicate Gather Intelligence; permits two different recall uses.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?
grades.expected: Winning respective Conflict puts control marker on flag replacing opponent. Controller receives 1 Solari at Arrakeen/Refinery or 1 spice at Basin whenever anyone including self visits. Reveal of controlled location Conflict permits one troop from supply directly to Conflict.

observed.answer: When a player visits a controlled critical location, the controller gets the location's bonus even if the controller is the visitor: Arrakeen or Spice Refinery gives 1 Solari, Imperial Basin gives 1 spice. Winning its named Conflict places your Control marker, replacing an opponent's. When its Conflict is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict.
observed.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; board-space table separates visitor and controller effects; Round Start defensive bonus.

grades.reason: Correct controller bonuses including self-visits, control replacement on winning named Conflict, and defensive troop from supply at reveal.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and the Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody wins or takes the card, and nobody else gets a reward (in either three- or four-player play).
observed.evidence: Combat ties and player-count table.

grades.reason: Correct tied-second third rewards with winner retained, no tied-third reward, and no winner/card/other rewards for three tied first.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: With three players and three different positive strengths, first and second place receive rewards; third gets nothing. The same applies in two-player play with its Rival as third competitor: ordinary first and second receive rewards, ordinary third does not, except third reward is used for a tie for second.
observed.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive rewards, third does not; Rival included.

grades.reason: Correct untied first/second-only rewards in three competitors, including the standard two-human-plus-Rival game.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; you may look at them, reveal only when played, and put resolved cards face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ—Draw timing: if Intrigue deck runs out, reshuffle discard.

grades.reason: The question asks when Combat Intrigues can be played. Phase timing alone omits the basic deployed-unit condition in the unchanged key/source. The NEW full10 grader and NEW neutral10 scope review treat this as material play permission, rather than an assertion of illegal play; no same-response statement/evidence supplies it. Earlier narrower phase-only judgments remain preserved.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies Intrigue; ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand. Secrets' separate steal effect takes one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
observed.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon threshold and random selection.

grades.reason: Correct hand-only ordinary discard excluding Intrigue and random theft from each opponent with four or more Intrigues.

grades.question: Which cards may a trash effect remove, where do ordinary and Reserve cards go, and is trashing optional? Does trashing The Spice Must Flow remove its acquired VP?
grades.expected: May trash own hand, discard or in-play card. Ordinary to box; Reserve back to its Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or direct self-trash. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained after trashing.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1185–1190; FAQ p4 The Spice Must Flow

observed.answer: Trashing can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play; return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card says to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquire VP; that VP is retained.
observed.evidence: Trashing section; FAQ—Victory: Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if later trashed.

grades.reason: Correct eligible trash locations, box versus Reserve destinations, optionality exceptions, and retained Spice Must Flow acquire VP.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

observed.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire the card. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot be saved.
observed.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; unused Persuasion lost.

grades.reason: Correct acquisition-time acquire effect, draw-triggered discard reshuffle, and expiration of unused Persuasion.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed first. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of the order played, provided each has another Fremen card in play. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to the discard pile.
observed.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen cards in play; reciprocal activation; Clean Up.

grades.reason: Correct Agent/Reveal cards in play until cleanup unless trashed and reciprocal Bond activation using another Fremen regardless of order.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1147–1157; FAQ p3 Retreat

observed.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent you sent that turn; it can be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
observed.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

grades.reason: Correct exclusion of current Agent from recall, later same-round reuse, retreat to garrison, and zero permitted by any number.

grades.question: When an effect grants two Influence with a freely chosen Faction, may it be split? What is required for an Alliance-icon effect or a minimum-Influence effect?
grades.expected: Choose one Faction, both Influence there (not split). Alliance effect requires holding shown Faction Alliance token; minimum-Influence effect requires at least shown value with shown Faction.

observed.answer: A free-choice gain of two Influence must go to one chosen Faction and cannot be split between two. Faction-specific icons apply only to their named Faction. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; an effect with a minimum Influence requirement requires meeting the named minimum.
observed.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two with one Faction; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

grades.reason: Correct indivisible two-Influence effect and named-Faction token/minimum requirements.

grades.question: If an Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, who receives the token? If the holder drops to 3 and no one has 4, what happens?
grades.expected: Former holder chooses one of previously tied opponents to receive token; holder loses Alliance VP and receiver gains it. Below 4 loses token; if no eligible 4+ player return token to board, losing its VP.

observed.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if multiple opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which receives it. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the Alliance to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence; FAQ—Alliance loss.

grades.reason: Correct former-holder choice among tied opponents and token return/lost VP below four when no eligible recipient exists.

grades.question: What happens to a card drawn during Reveal compared with one drawn after Reveal? What happens to a Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal?
grades.expected: During Reveal immediately reveal and use this turn; after Reveal keep until next round, then draw five extra. Plot effect for later Reveal stays face up until that Reveal, use then discard.

observed.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards then drawn. A Plot Intrigue played earlier that has a later Reveal effect remains face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
observed.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing.

grades.reason: Correct immediate Reveal draw use versus keeping post-Reveal draws plus next five and delayed Plot retention until used.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?
grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.
grades.source_references: FAQ p4 When you win a Conflict

observed.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
observed.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: win-trigger Intrigues cannot follow a first-place tie; if received as winning reward may be played immediately.

grades.reason: Correct denial of win-trigger Intrigue after a tie and permission for an appropriate card just gained from an outright win.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.
grades.source_references: FAQ p2 Endgame; p4 Victory Points

observed.answer: If final VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
observed.evidence: FAQ—Victory.

grades.reason: Correct latest-Reveal final tiebreak and scores above twelve.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?
grades.expected: Completion mandatory; all same-space contracts completed with one Agent placement. Their effects may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; still must hold them at placement.

observed.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement, and the contract must be held when sending the Agent. A board-space contract is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects.
observed.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory.

grades.reason: Correct mandatory completion of all held same-space contracts and freedom to order their effects with card/space effects.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.
grades.source_references: Main p17; FAQ p3 Shaddam Corrino IV

Emperor of the Known Universe applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, and restricts deployment for that turn only, not the whole round.
observed.evidence: FAQ—Shaddam.

grades.reason: Correct no starting possession of set-aside contracts, acquisition choice, and immediate turn-only Signet restriction.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.
grades.source_references: Main p17 / extraction 957–964; FAQ p3 Reverend Mother Jessica

observed.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may act on flip turn.

grades.reason: Correct Feyd initial/final token states, initial Lady Jessica side, and Reverend Mother ability on flip turn.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

observed.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 even when gaining multiple Influence at once. They can reach 2 again later by losing Influence and regaining it upward; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
observed.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

grades.reason: Correct upward crossing/repeat reach-two trigger, no downward trigger, and hand-only Spacing Guild Favor discard trigger.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract: Spice Trade, draw card plus contract or 2 Solari, no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service: Emperor, one Emperor Influence plus contract or 2 Solari. Contract fallback if module off or all contracts taken.

observed.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon and always draws one card; with CHOAM it also takes a contract, and without CHOAM or when none remain it gives 2 Solari instead. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, gives 1 Emperor Influence, and likewise takes a contract with CHOAM or gives 2 Solari without/no contracts. Neither space automatically gains Faction Influence from its access icon; Accept Contract gives no automatic Influence, while Dutiful's listed 1 Emperor Influence is an explicit effect.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide preface and Accept Contract/Dutiful Service rows.

grades.reason: The sentence 'Neither space automatically gains Faction Influence from its access icon' could be improved by saying that Dutiful Service's listed one Influence is its ordinary Faction-space advance. Read with its immediately stated one Emperor Influence and the explanation that this is listed explicitly, it conveys a single mandatory Influence gain, not zero and not a second gain in addition to the listed effect. The guide itself explicitly lists that gain. Calling the listed gain an explicit effect does not make it optional or deny its Faction-space origin. Unlike a claim that neither destination is a Faction space, this wording need not introduce a false classification. I therefore treat it as an awkward explanation of the correct requested comparison rather than impose an unspoken contradictory rule. No facts are borrowed from reader b or supplied by its bare citation.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.

Both also give all bonus spice present, including when choosing worms. Hooks are retained and not spent when summoning. Protected Conflicts at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin cannot receive a worm while the Shield Wall remains.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide rows; Makers; Sandworms/FAQ Hooks retained and Shield Wall.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option does not grant a troop.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr options and requirements.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council is Landsraad, not a Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council row.

grades.reason: Correct five-Solari visits, first Councilor and ongoing Reveal Persuasion versus later rewards, and noncombat status.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 Solari after anyone has one; each player may take it only once per game. Take your third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces human cost to 6.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster row.

grades.reason: Correct eight-to-six dynamic price including Rival trigger, once per player, and immediate same-round/rest-of-game Agent use.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege row; Recall Agent rule.

grades.reason: Correct Landsraad access, Emperor prerequisite, three-Solari cost, Intrigue exchange, other-Agent recall/card, and no automatic Emperor gain.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?
grades.expected: Each affected opponent moves Spy to empty observation post not connected to this turn Agent destination. Can play without enemy Spy there. Litany red box ignored during Reveal or with gained Agent icon when played normally as Agent card.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?
grades.expected: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.

observed.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.

Accept Contract/Shipping selection depends on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner depends on Conflict tier.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination conditions and occupied destination rule.

grades.question: A Rival has no troops newly recruited by a card sending it to Combat. Can it deploy garrison troops? What if a Hagal card recruits at a noncombat space or has a conditional 2-Influence bonus not met?
grades.expected: Still deploy up to two available garrison troops at Combat. New troops at noncombat go garrison. Missing 2-Influence bonus does not block placement, just no bonus. Use only Hagal effects, not ordinary board effects.

observed.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence is simply omitted if unmet; that does not prevent the Agent placement.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat spaces; conditional bonus does not prevent placement.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival puts a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

grades.reason: Correct priority Faction post selection, full-post omission, third-Spy recall/Scheme trigger, and no Rival Infiltrate/Gather.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before placement and the Rival reaches a Combat space that turn, deploy those Scheme-recruited troops too. If a Place Spy card has no legal empty post, ignore its placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
observed.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?
grades.expected: Always take bonus spice. With Hooks and summonable Conflict summons one at Hagga/two Deep instead of base. Without Hooks or if protected, summons none and gains base spice (2/4). At Imperial Basin gains base1. Hagal wall removal requires Hooks.

At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, with Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or when the Conflict is protected, it summons none and takes the base spice (Hagga 2; Deep Desert 4). Bonus spice is still collected in addition to that choice.
observed.evidence: Rival Maker spaces; Sandworm limitations; bonus spice collected.

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?
grades.expected: Start Combat in turn order, only with deployed unit: one Hagal card, bottom swords only added. Reshuffle and draw again on Reshuffle. Humans then Combat Intrigue before resolution. No unit no bonus.

If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
observed.evidence: Rival Combat.

grades.reason: Correct unit-required beginning-of-Combat bottom-swords reveal, Reshuffle redraw, human response window, and no unit-free bonus.

grades.question: Can a Rival gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and doubled rewards? How does it handle optional Conflict VP payments and contract rewards with CHOAM?
grades.expected: Normal control visit bonus and defensive supply troop; win card/match icons; sandworms double. Always buy optional Conflict VP if can pay resources or required Spy recall. Never contracts; each contract reward becomes 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

observed.answer: Yes: Rival receives normal placement rewards, may double rewards with worms, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, gets control bonuses on visits, and gets a defensive troop from supply when its controlled Conflict is revealed. It takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
